title: Selector agreement at zero
statement: Choose independent uniform bits $a,b\in\{0,1\}$ and independent uniform signs $x,y\in\{\pm1\}$. The printed selector agreement at zero is the probability that the Boolean samples selected from $a,b$ by $x$ and $y$ agree.
caveat: The definition of the Boolean sample selected by a sign is not included in the supplied statement, so its meaning cannot be specified more precisely.
